title: Victorian privacy regulator finds Education Department breached privacy law after school-system breach
date_note: OVIC's investigation report is dated October 2026 with no day given; iTnews reported its findings on 7 October 2026, the earliest dated page read. IDM reported the same findings on 20 November 2026. The breach was notified to OVIC on 7 January 2026.
summary: Victoria's privacy regulator OVIC found in its October 2026 report that the Department of Education contravened Information Privacy Principles 4.1 and 4.2. Through one school's compromised IT system, an attacker took every government school student's name, school, year level, school email and encrypted password, and those of hundreds of thousands of former students. OVIC made seven recommendations due by 31 December 2026; the department says it accepts them.
plain: Victoria's privacy regulator found the state education department kept former students' login data and did not protect student data well enough before a breach.
exec: Keeping credentials of past users and incomplete vulnerability remediation can breach privacy law.
action: OVIC recommended the department review its retention of past students' credentials and strengthen how critical vulnerability advisories reach schools; organisations holding similar records can run the same review.
impact: Former students affected: hundreds of thousands, per OVIC.

validation.note: OVIC's own report read (findings, recommendations and the department's response in Appendix A); iTnews and IDM report the findings.

review.note: title, IPP 4.1/4.2, seven recommendations due 31 Dec 2026, data fields, 7 Jan notification checked against IDM and iTnews; OVIC PDF could not be text-extracted so findings rest on the two press reports
